How much does a big CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md cost? Claude Code vs Codex

A 50 KB CLAUDE.md added 15,985 input tokens to every Claude Code request. Codex read only the first 32 KiB of a 50 KB AGENTS.md and silently ignored an instruction placed at the end. Claude Code’s prompt cache absorbs most of the cost after the first turn.

Measured 2026-10-18 · 6 file sizes · 2 tools · 2 runs · License CC BY 4.0 · Related: Claude Code vs Codex startup tokens

DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23453217 · Also on Hugging Face · Kaggle · GitHub

⬇ CSV ⬇ JSON How to cite

Key findings

  • Every kilobyte of CLAUDE.md costs about 320 input tokens on every request. With no instruction file, a one-word reply cost Claude Code 35,795 input tokens; a 10 KB CLAUDE.md added 3,303, a 25 KB file 8,080 and a 50 KB file 15,985 (+45%).
  • Codex stops reading AGENTS.md at 32 KiB. A 25 KB AGENTS.md added 5,339 tokens, but doubling it to 50 KB added only 1,495 more. We put the line “the release codename is BLUE-HERON-47” at the end of a 50 KB AGENTS.md: Codex answered “NONE” in 2 of 2 runs, while the same line at the start of the file was found 2 of 2 times. Codex documents this limit (project_doc_max_bytes, 32 KiB by default) but its output in our runs gave no warning that the file was cut.
  • Claude Code read the whole file. It found the codename at the start and at the end of the 50 KB CLAUDE.md in all 4 runs. Claude Code shows a performance warning for CLAUDE.md files over 40,000 characters but still loads them.
  • The cache makes the first turn the expensive one. At API list prices reported by Claude Code, the first request cost $0.162 with no file and $0.290 with the 50 KB file (+79%). On the second turn the file was read from the cache and the cost was $0.143 against $0.146 (+2%).
  • The same text costs Claude more tokens. The 25 KB file added 8,080 tokens in Claude Code and 5,339 in Codex, 51% more, in line with Claude’s tokenizer needing more tokens for the same English text.

Input tokens and cost by instruction file size

Prompt: “Reply with the single word OK.”, then “Reply with the single word OK again.” in the same session. Both runs gave identical token counts. Cost is the API list-price figure Claude Code reports (the runs used a Max plan); Codex does not report cost.

Is an instruction at the end of a big file followed?

A line “The release codename for this project is BLUE-HERON-47.” was added at the start or at the end of the 50 KB file, and each tool was asked for the codename without being allowed to open any files.

Method

  • The instruction files are a realistic project guide for a TypeScript monorepo (commands, then conventions for 60 modules), generated by a script so that the 1, 5, 10, 25 and 50 KB files are prefixes of the same text. The generator script is included in the JSON download.
  • The same file was saved as CLAUDE.md for Claude Code and AGENTS.md for Codex in an otherwise empty folder.
  • Claude Code 2.1.295 (Opus 5.5, effort medium): claude -p and then claude -c -p with --output-format json and no MCP servers. Input tokens are uncached input plus cache writes plus cache reads.
  • Codex CLI 0.162 (gpt-6-luna, effort medium): codex exec --json and then codex exec resume --last. Codex reports session totals, so turn 2 is the difference from turn 1.
  • Each configuration was run twice on 2026-10-18 on the same Windows laptop. The baseline includes each tool’s global settings on that machine, so only the added tokens should be compared.

Limitations

  • One kind of instruction text, English only; other languages need more tokens per kilobyte.
  • Sizes between 25 and 50 KB were not measured, so the exact point where Codex stops reading is taken from its documentation.
  • The cost figures are list-price estimates from Claude Code; subscription plans are not billed per token.
